questions.answer: Differentiate once: \(f'(x)=3x^2\). Differentiate again: \(f''(x)=6x\). Therefore the second derivative is \(6x\).
First differentiate term by term: \(f'(x)=16x^3-4x\). Differentiate the result: \(f''(x)=48x^2-4\). Therefore \(f''(x)=48x^2-4\).
Differentiate repeatedly. First, \(f'(x)=5x^4\). Second, \(f''(x)=20x^3\). Third, \(f^{(3)}(x)=60x^2\). Therefore the third derivative is \(60x^2\).
Velocity is the first derivative of position: \(s'(t)=3t^2-12t+4\). Acceleration is the second derivative: \(s''(t)=6t-12\). Therefore the acceleration function is \(6t-12\).
First differentiate: \(f'(x)=4x^3-3\). Differentiate again: \(f''(x)=12x^2\). Evaluate at \(x=1\): \(f''(1)=12(1)^2=12\).
Differentiate once: \(f'(x)=\cos x\). Differentiate again: the derivative of \(\cos x\) is \(-\sin x\). Therefore \(f''(x)=-\sin x\).
The derivative of \(e^x\) is always \(e^x\). Therefore \(f'(x)=e^x\), \(f''(x)=e^x\), \(f^{(3)}(x)=e^x\), and \(f^{(4)}(x)=e^x\).

First differentiate using the chain rule: \(f'(x)=3(x^2+1)^2\cdot2x=6x(x^2+1)^2\). Differentiate this product: \(f''(x)=6(x^2+1)^2+6x\cdot2(x^2+1)\cdot2x\). Simplify: \(f''(x)=6(x^2+1)^2+24x^2(x^2+1)=6(x^2+1)(5x^2+1)\).

questions.prompt: For \(f(x)=x^4-4x^3\), use \(f''(x)\) to determine where the graph is concave up.
questions.answer: First differentiate: \(f'(x)=4x^3-12x^2\). Differentiate again: \(f''(x)=12x^2-24x=12x(x-2)\). The graph is concave up where \(f''(x)>0\). The product \(12x(x-2)\) is positive when \(x<0\) or \(x>2\). Therefore the graph is concave up on \(( -\infty,0)\cup(2,\infty)\).

questions.prompt: Find a formula for \(f^{(n)}(x)\) when \(f(x)=x^5\) for \(n=1,2,3,4,5\).
questions.answer: Differentiate repeatedly and track the pattern. First: \(f'(x)=5x^4\). Second: \(f''(x)=20x^3\). Third: \(f^{(3)}(x)=60x^2\). Fourth: \(f^{(4)}(x)=120x\). Fifth: \(f^{(5)}(x)=120\). Each step lowers the power by \(1\) and multiplies by the previous power.
